question: Can you calculate the 5-day symmetric moving average of predicted toy sales for December 5 to 8, 2018, using daily sales data from January 1, 2017, to August 29, 2018, with a simple linear regression model? Finally provide the sum of those four 5-day moving averages?
pred_sql:
WITH
-- 1. Prepare daily sales for toys between 2017-01-01 and 2018-08-29
daily_sales AS (
    SELECT
        date(o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS sale_date,
        COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS orders_count
    FROM orders o
    JOIN order_items oi USING(order_id)
    JOIN products p USING(product_id)
    WHERE date(o.order_purchase_timestamp) BETWEEN '2017-01-01' AND '2018-08-29'
      AND p.product_category_name LIKE '%toy%' -- match toy category (adjust if different)
      AND o.order_status = 'delivered'
    GROUP BY date(o.order_purchase_timestamp)
),
-- 2. Create a continuous date series for the training period to ensure zero-sales days included
dates AS (
    SELECT date('2017-01-01', '+' || (n) || ' days') AS dt
    FROM (
        SELECT row_number() OVER () - 1 AS n
        FROM (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1) a,
             (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1) b,
             (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1) c,
             (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 1) d
    )
    WHERE date('2017-01-01', '+' || n || ' days') <= date('2018-08-29')
),
train AS (
    SELECT
        dt AS sale_date,
        COALESCE(ds.orders_count, 0) AS sales,
        -- day index as numeric independent variable for linear regression
        CAST(julianday(dt) - julianday('2017-01-01') AS REAL) AS day_index
    FROM dates dt
    LEFT JOIN daily_sales ds ON ds.sale_date = dt
),
-- 3. Compute linear regression coefficients (slope and intercept) using least squares
stats AS (
    SELECT
        COUNT(*) AS n,
        SUM(day_index) AS sum_x,
        SUM(sales) AS sum_y,
        SUM(day_index * sales) AS sum_xy,
        SUM(day_index * day_index) AS sum_x2
    FROM train
),
coeffs AS (
    SELECT
        (n * sum_xy - sum_x * sum_y) / (n * sum_x2 - sum_x * sum_x) AS slope,
        (sum_y - ((n * sum_xy - sum_x * sum_y) / (n * sum_x2 - sum_x * sum_x)) * sum_x) / n AS intercept
    FROM stats
),
-- 4. Define prediction dates (2018-12-05 to 2018-12-08) and compute predicted sales via the regression model.
pred_dates AS (
    SELECT date('2018-12-05', '+' || (i) || ' days') AS pred_date
    FROM (SELECT 0 AS i UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3)
),
predictions AS (
    SELECT
        pd.pred_date,
        -- compute day_index relative to training origin
        CAST(julianday(pd.pred_date) - julianday('2017-01-01') AS REAL) AS day_index,
        c.slope,
        c.intercept,
        -- predicted sales from linear model
        (c.intercept + c.slope * (julianday(pd.pred_date) - julianday('2017-01-01'))) AS predicted_sales
    FROM pred_dates pd
    CROSS JOIN coeffs c
),
-- 5. To compute 5-day symmetric moving average for each prediction date, gather predictions for date-2..date+2.
pred_neighbors AS (
    SELECT
        p.pred_date,
        AVG(p2.predicted_sales) AS moving_avg_5
    FROM predictions p
    JOIN predictions p2
      ON julianday(p2.pred_date) BETWEEN julianday(p.pred_date, '-2 days') AND julianday(p.pred_date, '+2 days')
    GROUP BY p.pred_date
)
-- 6. Sum the four 5-day moving averages
SELECT ROUND(SUM(moving_avg_5), 4) AS sum_of_4_moving_averages
FROM pred_neighbors

question: According to the RFM definition document, calculate the average sales per order for each customer within distinct RFM segments, considering only 'delivered' orders. Use the customer unique identifier. Clearly define how to calculate Recency based on the latest purchase timestamp and specify the criteria for classifying RFM segments. The average sales should be computed as the total spend divided by the total number of orders. Please analyze and report the differences in average sales across the RFM segments
pred_sql:
-- Calculate R, F, M scores by quintiles, assign RFM segment, then compute average sales per order per segment
WITH delivered_orders AS (
    SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.order_purchase_timestamp
    FROM orders o
    WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
),
payments_per_order AS (
    SELECT op.order_id,
           SUM(op.payment_value) AS order_payment
    FROM order_payments op
    GROUP BY op.order_id
),
customer_metrics AS (
    -- For each customer_unique_id compute Recency (days since last purchase relative to max purchase in data),
    -- Frequency (count of delivered orders), Monetary (total spend across delivered orders)
    SELECT
        c.customer_unique_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT do.order_id) AS frequency,
        SUM(p.order_payment) AS monetary,
        MAX(do.order_purchase_timestamp) AS last_purchase_ts
    FROM customers c
    JOIN delivered_orders do ON c.customer_id = do.customer_id
    JOIN payments_per_order p ON do.order_id = p.order_id
    GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id
),
global_reference AS (
    -- reference date = latest purchase timestamp in dataset (to compute recency in days)
    SELECT MAX(last_purchase_ts) AS reference_ts FROM customer_metrics
),
customer_with_recency AS (
    SELECT
        cm.*,
        -- recency in days: difference between reference date and customer's last purchase
        JULIANDAY(gr.reference_ts) - JULIANDAY(cm.last_purchase_ts) AS recency_days
    FROM customer_metrics cm CROSS JOIN global_reference gr
),
percentiles AS (
    -- compute quintile borders for recency (lower is better => we will invert scores),
    -- frequency and monetary (higher is better)
    SELECT
        -- recency borders
        MAX(CASE WHEN p = 0.2 THEN value END) AS r_20,
        MAX(CASE WHEN p = 0.4 THEN value END) AS r_40,
        MAX(CASE WHEN p = 0.6 THEN value END) AS r_60,
        MAX(CASE WHEN p = 0.8 THEN value END) AS r_80,
        -- frequency borders
        MAX(CASE WHEN p = 0.2 THEN freq_val END) AS f_20,
        MAX(CASE WHEN p = 0.4 THEN freq_val END) AS f_40,
        MAX(CASE WHEN p = 0.6 THEN freq_val END) AS f_60,
        MAX(CASE WHEN p = 0.8 THEN freq_val END) AS f_80,
        -- monetary borders
        MAX(CASE WHEN p = 0.2 THEN mon_val END) AS m_20,
        MAX(CASE WHEN p = 0.4 THEN mon_val END) AS m_40,
        MAX(CASE WHEN p = 0.6 THEN mon_val END) AS m_60,
        MAX(CASE WHEN p = 0.8 THEN mon_val END) AS m_80
    FROM (
        -- unpivot the distributions into percentile rows using row_number over ordered values to approximate quantiles
        SELECT value, NULL AS freq_val, NULL AS mon_val, p FROM (
            SELECT recency_days AS value,
                   (CAST(ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY recency_days) AS REAL) / COUNT(*) OVER ()) AS p
            FROM customer_with_recency
        )
        UNION ALL
        SELECT NULL AS value, value_f AS freq_val, NULL AS mon_val, p FROM (
            SELECT frequency AS value_f,
                   (CAST(ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY frequency) AS REAL) / COUNT(*) OVER ()) AS p
            FROM customer_with_recency
        )
        UNION ALL
        SELECT NULL AS value, NULL AS freq_val, value_m AS mon_val, p FROM (
            SELECT monetary AS value_m,
                   (CAST(ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY monetary) AS REAL) / COUNT(*) OVER ()) AS p
            FROM customer_with_recency
        )
    )
),
rfm_scored AS (
    SELECT
        cwr.customer_unique_id,
        cwr.recency_days,
        cwr.frequency,
        cwr.monetary,
        -- Recency score: 1 (best) to 5 (worst) by quintiles; since lower recency_days is better, invert the mapping
        CASE
            WHEN cwr.recency_days <= COALESCE(p.r_20, cwr.recency_days) THEN 1
            WHEN cwr.recency_days <= COALESCE(p.r_40, cwr.recency_days) THEN 2
            WHEN cwr.recency_days <= COALESCE(p.r_60, cwr.recency_days) THEN 3
            WHEN cwr.recency_days <= COALESCE(p.r_80, cwr.recency_days) THEN 4
            ELSE 5
        END AS R,
        -- Frequency score: higher frequency is better => 1 (best/highest freq) to 5 (worst/lowest freq)
        CASE
            WHEN cwr.frequency > COALESCE(p.f_80, cwr.frequency) THEN 1
            WHEN cwr.frequency > COALESCE(p.f_60, cwr.frequency) THEN 2
            WHEN cwr.frequency > COALESCE(p.f_40, cwr.frequency) THEN 3
            WHEN cwr.frequency > COALESCE(p.f_20, cwr.frequency) THEN 4
            ELSE 5
        END AS F,
        -- Monetary score: higher monetary is better => 1 (best/highest spend) to 5 (worst)
        CASE
            WHEN cwr.monetary > COALESCE(p.m_80, cwr.monetary) THEN 1
            WHEN cwr.monetary > COALESCE(p.m_60, cwr.monetary) THEN 2
            WHEN cwr.monetary > COALESCE(p.m_40, cwr.monetary) THEN 3
            WHEN cwr.monetary > COALESCE(p.m_20, cwr.monetary) THEN 4
            ELSE 5
        END AS M
    FROM customer_with_recency cwr
    CROSS JOIN percentiles p
),
rfm_segment AS (
    -- define segments by concatenating R,F,M scores (e.g., '111' best, '555' worst)
    SELECT
        r.*,
        CAST(R AS TEXT) || CAST(F AS TEXT) || CAST(M AS TEXT) AS rfm_cell
    FROM rfm_scored r
),
avg_sales_per_customer AS (
    -- average sales per order per customer (monetary / frequency)
    SELECT
        rfm.customer_unique_id,
        rfm.rfm_cell,
        CASE WHEN frequency = 0 THEN 0 ELSE monetary / frequency END AS avg_sales_per_order
    FROM rfm_segment rfm
)
-- final: average of avg_sales_per_order grouped by RFM cell, and count of customers per cell for context
SELECT
    rfm_cell,
    COUNT(*) AS customers_in_segment,
    ROUND(AVG(avg_sales_per_order), 2) AS avg_sales_per_order_mean,
    ROUND(MAX(avg_sales_per_order) - MIN(avg_sales_per_order), 2) AS range_avg_sales_per_order
FROM avg_sales_per_customer
GROUP BY rfm_cell
ORDER BY rfm_cell

question: Could you help me calculate the average single career span value in years for all baseball players? Please precise the result as a float number. First, calculate the difference in years, months, and days between the debut and final game dates. For each player, the career span is computed as the sum of the absolute number of years, plus the absolute number of months divided by 12, plus the absolute number of days divided by 365. Round each part to two decimal places before summing. Finally, average the career spans and round the result to a float number.
pred_sql:
WITH parsed AS (
  SELECT
    player_id,
    debut,
    final_game,
    -- parse dates into components (nullable)
    CASE WHEN debut IS NOT NULL AND debut <> '' THEN CAST(substr(debut,1,4) AS INTEGER) END AS d_y,
    CASE WHEN debut IS NOT NULL AND debut <> '' THEN CAST(substr(debut,6,2) AS INTEGER) END AS d_m,
    CASE WHEN debut IS NOT NULL AND debut <> '' THEN CAST(substr(debut,9,2) AS INTEGER) END AS d_d,
    CASE WHEN final_game IS NOT NULL AND final_game <> '' THEN CAST(substr(final_game,1,4) AS INTEGER) END AS f_y,
    CASE WHEN final_game IS NOT NULL AND final_game <> '' THEN CAST(substr(final_game,6,2) AS INTEGER) END AS f_m,
    CASE WHEN final_game IS NOT NULL AND final_game <> '' THEN CAST(substr(final_game,9,2) AS INTEGER) END AS f_d
  FROM player
),
diffs AS (
  SELECT
    player_id,
    d_y,d_m,d_d,f_y,f_m,f_d,
    -- only keep rows with valid parsed dates
    CASE
      WHEN d_y IS NULL OR f_y IS NULL THEN NULL
      ELSE ABS(f_y - d_y)
    END AS years_diff,
    CASE
      WHEN d_m IS NULL OR f_m IS NULL THEN NULL
      ELSE ABS(f_m - d_m)
    END AS months_diff,
    CASE
      WHEN d_d IS NULL OR f_d IS NULL THEN NULL
      ELSE ABS(f_d - d_d)
    END AS days_diff
  FROM parsed
),
rounded_parts AS (
  SELECT
    player_id,
    years_diff,
    months_diff,
    days_diff,
    -- round each part to 2 decimals as specified
    CASE WHEN years_diff IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE ROUND(CAST(years_diff AS REAL),2) END AS years_part,
    CASE WHEN months_diff IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE ROUND(CAST(months_diff AS REAL)/12.0,2) END AS months_part,
    CASE WHEN days_diff IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE ROUND(CAST(days_diff AS REAL)/365.0,2) END AS days_part
  FROM diffs
),
career_spans AS (
  SELECT
    player_id,
    -- only include players with all three parts non-null
    (years_part + months_part + days_part) AS career_span
  FROM rounded_parts
  WHERE years_part IS NOT NULL AND months_part IS NOT NULL AND days_part IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT CAST(ROUND(AVG(career_span), 2) AS REAL) AS average_career_span_years
FROM career_spans

question: What is the distance of the longest route where Abakan is either the departure or destination city (in kilometers)?

WITH abakan_airports AS (
  SELECT airport_code, (json_extract(city, '$.en')) AS city_name, 
         -- coordinates is a point type; in sqlite it's stored like "(lon,lat)". Extract numbers.
         CAST(trim(substr(coordinates, 2, instr(coordinates, ',')-2)) AS REAL) AS lon,
         CAST(trim(substr(coordinates, instr(coordinates, ',')+1, length(coordinates)-instr(coordinates, ',')-1)) AS REAL) AS lat
  FROM airports_data
  WHERE json_extract(city, '$.en') = 'Abakan'
),
route_pairs AS (
  SELECT f.flight_id,
         f.departure_airport, f.arrival_airport,
         da.lat AS dep_lat, da.lon AS dep_lon,
         aa.lat AS arr_lat, aa.lon AS arr_lon
  FROM flights f
  JOIN abakan_airports da ON f.departure_airport = da.airport_code
  JOIN airports_data a ON f.arrival_airport = a.airport_code
  -- extract arrival coords
  JOIN (
    SELECT airport_code,
           CAST(trim(substr(coordinates, 2, instr(coordinates, ',')-2)) AS REAL) AS lon,
           CAST(trim(substr(coordinates, instr(coordinates, ',')+1, length(coordinates)-instr(coordinates, ',')-1)) AS REAL) AS lat
    FROM airports_data
  ) aa ON aa.airport_code = a.airport_code

  UNION

  SELECT f.flight_id,
         f.departure_airport, f.arrival_airport,
         da.lat AS dep_lat, da.lon AS dep_lon,
         aa.lat AS arr_lat, aa.lon AS arr_lon
  FROM flights f
  JOIN abakan_airports aa ON f.arrival_airport = aa.airport_code
  JOIN airports_data d ON f.departure_airport = d.airport_code
  JOIN (
    SELECT airport_code,
           CAST(trim(substr(coordinates, 2, instr(coordinates, ',')-2)) AS REAL) AS lon,
           CAST(trim(substr(coordinates, instr(coordinates, ',')+1, length(coordinates)-instr(coordinates, ',')-1)) AS REAL) AS lat
    FROM airports_data
  ) da ON da.airport_code = d.airport_code
),
haversine AS (
  SELECT *,
    -- convert degrees to radians
    ( (dep_lat * pi()/180.0) ) AS dep_lat_rad,
    ( (dep_lon * pi()/180.0) ) AS dep_lon_rad,
    ( (arr_lat * pi()/180.0) ) AS arr_lat_rad,
    ( (arr_lon * pi()/180.0) ) AS arr_lon_rad
  FROM route_pairs
),
distances AS (
  SELECT *,
    -- Haversine formula
    2 * 6371.0 * asin(
      sqrt(
        power(sin((arr_lat_rad - dep_lat_rad)/2.0), 2)
        + cos(dep_lat_rad) * cos(arr_lat_rad) * power(sin((arr_lon_rad - dep_lon_rad)/2.0), 2)
      )
    ) AS distance_km
  FROM haversine
)
SELECT MAX(distance_km) AS longest_distance_km
FROM distances

question: Distribute all the unique city pairs into the distance ranges 0, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000, and 6000+, based on their average distance of all routes between them. Then how many pairs are there in the distance range with the fewest unique city paires?
pred_sql:
WITH
-- extract cities (english name) and coordinates for each airport
airp AS (
  SELECT
    airport_code,
    json_extract(city, '$.en') AS city,
    CAST(substr(trim(printf('%.15g', coordinates)), 2, instr(trim(printf('%.15g', coordinates)), ',')-2) AS REAL) AS lon,
    CAST(substr(trim(printf('%.15g', coordinates)), instr(trim(printf('%.15g', coordinates)), ',')+1,
                length(trim(printf('%.15g', coordinates))) - instr(trim(printf('%.15g', coordinates)), ',') -1) AS REAL) AS lat
  FROM airports_data
),
-- pair each flight with from/to city names and coords
flight_cities AS (
  SELECT
    f.flight_id,
    af.city AS from_city,
    af.lon AS from_lon,
    af.lat AS from_lat,
    at.city AS to_city,
    at.lon AS to_lon,
    at.lat AS to_lat
  FROM flights f
  JOIN airp af ON f.departure_airport = af.airport_code
  JOIN airp at ON f.arrival_airport = at.airport_code
  WHERE af.city IS NOT NULL AND at.city IS NOT NULL
),
-- haversine distance in kilometers per flight
flight_dist AS (
  SELECT
    flight_id,
    from_city,
    to_city,
    -- convert degrees to radians
    2.0 * 6371.0 * ASIN(
      SQRT(
        POWER(SIN(( (from_lat - to_lat) * PI()/180.0 )/2.0), 2)
        +
        COS(from_lat * PI()/180.0) * COS(to_lat * PI()/180.0)
        * POWER(SIN(( (from_lon - to_lon) * PI()/180.0 )/2.0), 2)
      )
    ) AS distance_km
  FROM flight_cities
),
-- normalize city pair so (A,B) and (B,A) are same
norm_pairs AS (
  SELECT
    flight_id,
    CASE WHEN from_city <= to_city THEN from_city ELSE to_city END AS city_a,
    CASE WHEN from_city <= to_city THEN to_city ELSE from_city END AS city_b,
    distance_km
  FROM flight_dist
  WHERE from_city IS NOT NULL AND to_city IS NOT NULL AND from_city <> to_city
),
-- average distance per unique city pair
pair_avg AS (
  SELECT
    city_a,
    city_b,
    AVG(distance_km) AS avg_km
  FROM norm_pairs
  GROUP BY city_a, city_b
),
-- bucket into ranges: 0-999 -> 0, 1000-1999 ->1000, ... 5000-5999 ->5000, >=6000 ->6000
pair_bucket AS (
  SELECT
    city_a, city_b, avg_km,
    CASE
      WHEN avg_km < 1000 THEN 0
      WHEN avg_km < 2000 THEN 1000
      WHEN avg_km < 3000 THEN 2000
      WHEN avg_km < 4000 THEN 3000
      WHEN avg_km < 5000 THEN 4000
      WHEN avg_km < 6000 THEN 5000
      ELSE 6000
    END AS bucket_start
  FROM pair_avg
),
-- count pairs per bucket
counts AS (
  SELECT bucket_start, COUNT(*) AS pairs_count
  FROM pair_bucket
  GROUP BY bucket_start
)
-- find the minimal count and return that number
SELECT COALESCE(MIN(pairs_count), 0) AS fewest_pairs_count
FROM counts

Specifically, calculate two percentages: 1) the percentage of motorcyclist fatalities in collisions where parties (drivers or passengers) were wearing helmets, and 2) the percentage of motorcyclist fatalities in collisions where parties were not wearing helmets. WITH -- mark parties as helmeted or not based on party_safety_equipment_1 or _2 containing 'helmet'

  SELECT

    party_number,

      WHEN LOWER(COALESCE(party_safety_equipment_1,'') ) LIKE '%helmet%' OR LOWER(COALESCE(party_safety_equipment_2,'')) LIKE '%helmet%' THEN 'helmet'
      WHEN (LOWER(COALESCE(party_safety_equipment_1,'')) <> '' OR LOWER(COALESCE(party_safety_equipment_2,'')) <> '') AND
           LOWER(COALESCE(party_safety_equipment_1,'')) NOT LIKE '%helmet%' AND LOWER(COALESCE(party_safety_equipment_2,'')) NOT LIKE '%helmet%' THEN 'no_helmet'
      ELSE 'unknown'
    END AS helmet_status
  FROM parties

-- identify collisions that involve at least one motorcycle (motorcycle_collision flag) and join collisions -> we will count collisions per helmet group if any party in that collision falls in the group
coll_with_flag AS (
  SELECT
    c.case_id,
    c.motorcycle_collision
  FROM collisions c

),
-- collisions that have at least one party helmet / no_helmet

    MAX(CASE WHEN ph.helmet_status = 'no_helmet' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_nohelmet_party

-- total collisions involving motorcycles and having helmeted parties (count each collision once if it has any helmeted party)
collisions_by_group AS (

question: Provide the full names of drivers who have been overtaken on track more times than they have overtaken others on track during race laps, excluding position changes due to pit stops (both at pit entry and exit), retirements, or position changes that occurred during the first lap of a race (considered as start movements).

WITH lp AS (
  SELECT race_id, driver_id, lap, position
  FROM lap_positions
  WHERE lap IS NOT NULL
),
-- identify laps that are pit-in or pit-out by checking if there's any pit_stop for that driver at that lap
pit_laps AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT race_id, driver_id, lap
  FROM pit_stops
  WHERE lap IS NOT NULL
),
-- identify retirement laps to exclude them (if retirement row exists for that driver/race)
ret_laps AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT race_id, driver_id, lap
  FROM retirements
  WHERE lap IS NOT NULL
),
-- for each driver and race and lap > 1 and not a pit lap and not a retirement lap, get position change compared to previous lap
pos_changes AS (
  SELECT
    cur.race_id,
    cur.driver_id,
    cur.lap,
    prev.position AS pos_prev,
    cur.position AS pos_cur,
    (prev.position - cur.position) AS delta -- positive => improved (overtook someone); negative => was overtaken
  FROM lp cur
  JOIN lp prev
    ON cur.race_id = prev.race_id
   AND cur.driver_id = prev.driver_id
   AND cur.lap = prev.lap + 1
  LEFT JOIN pit_laps pl ON cur.race_id = pl.race_id AND cur.driver_id = pl.driver_id AND cur.lap = pl.lap
  LEFT JOIN pit_laps pl_prev ON prev.race_id = pl_prev.race_id AND prev.driver_id = pl_prev.driver_id AND prev.lap = prev.lap
  LEFT JOIN ret_laps rl ON cur.race_id = rl.race_id AND cur.driver_id = rl.driver_id AND cur.lap = rl.lap
  LEFT JOIN ret_laps rl_prev ON prev.race_id = rl_prev.race_id AND prev.driver_id = rl_prev.driver_id AND prev.lap = prev.lap
  WHERE cur.lap > 1
    AND pl.race_id IS NULL    -- exclude laps where a pit stop happened at this lap (pit entry/exit)
    AND pl_prev.race_id IS NULL -- exclude laps where a pit stop happened at previous lap
    AND rl.race_id IS NULL    -- exclude laps that are retirement laps
    AND rl_prev.race_id IS NULL
),
-- count overtakes and times overtaken per driver across all races/laps (overtake: delta>0, overtaken: delta<0)
counts AS (
  SELECT
    driver_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN delta > 0 THEN delta ELSE 0 END) AS overtakes_made,
    SUM(CASE WHEN delta < 0 THEN -delta ELSE 0 END) AS times_overtaken
  FROM pos_changes
  GROUP BY driver_id

FROM counts c
JOIN drivers d ON c.driver_id = d.driver_id
